scope.question: Is a model-specific, hardware-through-serving co-design simulator and autoresearch loop a defensible business wedge for lower input- and output-token inference cost?
scope.supported_claim: Primary-source snapshot of publicly documented competitive capabilities, validation methods, and proposed falsification gates as of the stated date.
unsupported_claims: competitor performance reproduced by Inference Foundry
measured input- or output-token cost advantage
custom silicon readiness or tapeout economics

evidence_policy.vendor_statement_treatment: A vendor page or blog establishes that the vendor publicly makes the statement, not that the claimed performance is independently true.
evidence_policy.paper_result_treatment: A primary paper establishes an author-reported method and result until an independent implementation reproduces it.
evidence_policy.public_repository_treatment: An inspectable repository establishes public artifact availability and documented scope, not accuracy on our models or workloads.
evidence_policy.absence_treatment: A capability not demonstrated in the reviewed public sources is not treated as proof that a competitor lacks it internally.
evidence_policy.analysis_inference_treatment: Competitive implications, commoditization labels, the surviving wedge and decision thresholds are analyst inferences or proposed tests, not direct source claims.

entries.name: NVIDIA DynoSim plus AIConfigurator

public_claims.statement: NVIDIA documents a workload-driven discrete-event twin of Dynamo that composes engine scheduling, Router, Planner, KV-cache behavior, traces, and AIC-backed pass timing, and directs users to validate shortlisted configurations on real GPUs.
NVIDIA reports that its Rust offline replay simulated a 23,608-request, 60.1-minute Mooncake trace in 2.41 seconds on an Apple M4, approximately 1,500x faster than real time.

The AIConfigurator authors report primitive-decomposed, calibrated multi-framework performance modeling, searches averaging under 30 seconds, and selected configurations improving dense-model performance by up to 40% and MoE performance by up to 50% on their evaluated workloads.

entries.competitive_implication: Full-stack serving DES, calibrated pass timing, Pareto sweeps, and a Rust implementation are already a public incumbent capability and cannot be the wedge by themselves.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The reviewed sources focus on deployment choices for supported model/backend/GPU tuples and explicitly retain real-hardware validation; they do not independently prove arbitrary model-architecture or custom-silicon predictions.

entries.name: NVIDIA hardware-friendly model co-design

public_claims.statement: NVIDIA publicly recommends dimensions aligned to at least 128 and preferably 256 or 512, fewer larger operations where quality permits, low-precision-friendly layers, repeatable pipeline-balanced layer patterns, wide expert parallelism, and decoupled attention and FFN parallelism.

NVIDIA describes LatentMoE as a hardware-software co-design that contracts routed experts into a latent space to reduce expert-weight traffic and all-to-all payload while reinvesting savings in expert capacity.

entries.competitive_implication: Hardware-aware model geometry, precision, sparsity, and parallelism co-design are publicly articulated and used in released model families; model modification alone is not an empty competitive category.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The sources provide vendor design guidance and vendor-reported model results, not an independently reproduced autonomous search loop or proof that the rules generalize to GLM architectures.

entries.name: Fireworks FireOptimizer and 3D FireOptimizer

public_claims.statement: Fireworks says FireOptimizer adapts hardware mapping, model quantization or tuning, caching and request handling, and specialized speculative models to workload data and latency, quality, and cost goals.
Fireworks reports adaptive speculative execution delivering up to 3x latency improvement and gives one vendor case with a 76% draft hit rate and 2x speed increase versus no speculation.

Fireworks says 3D FireOptimizer searches a space exceeding 100,000 combinations across model architecture, quantization, speculation, hardware, parallelism, and disaggregation, using production profiles and heuristics to find workload- and SLA-specific Pareto configurations.

entries.competitive_implication: Workload-specific search across hardware, model, speculation, quantization, and serving is commercially occupied and directly overlaps an ordinary full-stack optimization service.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The case studies and speedups are vendor reports without raw configurations, independent reruns, or a public general simulator contract.

entries.name: Etched frontier inference clusters

public_claims.statement: Etched says it co-designs chips, packages, racks, software, manufacturing methods, cooling, power delivery, interconnects, tiling, and scheduling for frontier-model inference.
Etched states that A0 silicon returned from TSMC N4P, a first rack-scale product is under customer validation, and racks have been tested in representative data centers.
Etched says it has run terabytes of production traffic patterns through an internal simulator while co-designing its rack-scale product.

entries.competitive_implication: Chip-to-rack-to-software verticality and simulator-guided custom hardware are already competitively occupied, even if Etched does not expose its internal simulator as a public product in the reviewed page.
entries.public_evidence_limit: LVI, cluster-scale memory, performance, demand, shipment, and production statements are vendor claims; no public independent benchmark or simulator input/output contract is provided on the reviewed page.

entries.name: Furiosa RNGD accelerator and per-model compiler stack

public_claims.statement: Furiosa documents a model-enablement path in which TCL kernels compile to executable binaries, SDK 2026.3 ships per-model FXB bundles, and the stack targets its RNGD Tensor Contraction Processor accelerator.
Furiosa says ArtifactBuilder applies expert-tuned per-model prefill and decode bucket presets during compilation to automate model-specific performance tuning.
Furiosa reports a 74.9% average throughput improvement for Qwen3 and EXAONE 4.0 families in SDK 2026.2 versus its previous SDK, combining compiler changes and hybrid KV-cache management.

entries.competitive_implication: Per-model compiler artifacts, kernel enablement, model presets, a custom accelerator, and an integrated serving stack are already a shipping competitive pattern; per-model specialization alone is not a wedge.
entries.public_evidence_limit: Performance deltas, production status, and hardware efficiency remain vendor-reported, and the reviewed sources do not expose an independently executable full hardware simulator.

entries.name: ASTRA-sim

public_claims.statement: The public ASTRA-sim repository documents a distributed-AI simulator spanning workload scheduling, collective algorithms, and compute, memory, and network hardware with plug-in APIs and Chakra traces.
The ASTRA-sim 3.0 authors report cache-line-granularity load/store simulation, a detailed GPU execution model, and InfraGraph for higher-fidelity infrastructure representation.

entries.competitive_implication: Distributed compute, memory, topology, and collective simulation are open building blocks rather than a proprietary wedge.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The repository landing page still labels the current project ASTRA-sim 2.0 while the newer 3.0 paper describes additions; neither source establishes accuracy for our inference models without calibration and execution.

entries.name: Timeloop and Accelergy

public_claims.statement: Timeloop v4 publicly documents analytical tensor-algebra architecture modeling and mapper search over dataflows and mappings for parameterized compute and memory hierarchies.
The v4 output contract documents mappings, cycles, throughput, access counts, energy and area statistics, plus Accelergy energy and area reference tables.

entries.competitive_implication: Tensor mapping, memory-traffic, cycle, energy, and area exploration are open infrastructure; differentiation must come from validated model and serving integration, not recreating a mapper contract.
entries.public_evidence_limit: Analytical outputs depend on architecture, mapping, technology and plug-in assumptions and require validation against silicon or lower-level tools before supporting cost claims.

entries.name: LLMServingSim 2.0

public_claims.statement: The public project documents a vLLM-like continuous-batching frontend, ASTRA-sim network backend, layerwise hardware profiles, heterogeneous accelerators, disaggregated CPU/CXL/PIM memory, MoE routing, and TP, PP, EP and DP multi-instance simulation.
The authors report average 0.97% error against real deployments for selected performance, memory, and power metrics and simulation times around 10 minutes for complex configurations.

entries.competitive_implication: Heterogeneous and disaggregated LLM serving co-simulation is an open research baseline that substantially overlaps the proposed simulation environment.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The accuracy and runtime numbers are author-reported and profile-dependent; this landscape did not execute the project or validate arbitrary model architecture mutations.

entries.name: MLPerf Inference

public_claims.statement: MLCommons documents architecture-neutral inference scenarios, LoadGen query scheduling and latency collection, accuracy validation, power submissions, closed and open divisions, availability categories, and submission checking.

entries.competitive_implication: A credible hardware or provider claim should adopt MLPerf-style frozen accuracy, load generation, system disclosure, power measurement, and result checking even when the exact research model is not an MLPerf closed-division model.
entries.public_evidence_limit: Inference Foundry has not completed or submitted an MLPerf result, and an internal benchmark using similar controls is not an MLPerf result.

entries.name: AA-AgentPerf

public_claims.statement: Artificial Analysis documents sustained concurrent agents replaying real multi-turn coding trajectories with tool calls, approximately 5K to 131K input lengths, model-specific TTFT and output-speed SLO tiers, measured accelerator power, and maximum-agent and output-throughput results normalized per accelerator, system and MW.

entries.competitive_implication: The intended agent-heavy pricing workload now has a concrete external validation target; uniform synthetic token traces are insufficient for business promotion.
entries.public_evidence_limit: Inference Foundry has not run AA-AgentPerf, Artificial Analysis controls the current dataset and publication process, and methodology adoption alone does not create an official result.

entries.name: IndexCache cross-layer DSA index reuse

public_claims.statement: The authors report that reusing DSA top-k selections across layers removes up to 75% of indexer computation, reaches up to 1.82x prefill and 1.48x decode speedup on a 30B DSA model, and has preliminary production-scale GLM-5 evidence.

entries.competitive_implication: Cross-layer DSA sharing is published research and is already trained into GLM-5.2 as IndexShare, so it is a baseline mechanism rather than a new model-specific wedge.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The reported speedups are author measurements on disclosed study settings, not a local GLM-5.2 reproduction or delivered cost result.

entries.name: TISA temporal DSA score reuse

public_claims.statement: The authors report round-robin refresh of cached DSA scores with K in 2, 4 and 8, competitive LongBench and retrieval results on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5, and 3.8x to 7.3x indexer-kernel speedup on H20.

entries.competitive_implication: Temporal score reuse is already a published GLM-adjacent mechanism and can compose with IndexShare, so an equivalent cache alone would not be novel.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The reviewed submission is author-reported, uses GLM-5 rather than GLM-5.2, and does not establish agent-task quality or end-to-end cost.

entries.name: HISA hierarchical DSA indexing

public_claims.statement: The authors report a training-free two-stage DSA indexer that prunes blocks before token refinement, exceeds 99% mean selected-set IoU, and reaches 2x kernel speedup at 32K and 4x at 128K on their DeepSeek-V3.2 study.

entries.competitive_implication: Hierarchical index pruning is already an explicit DSA optimization baseline that a GLM-specific search must compare against.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The result is not a GLM-5.2 measurement, was not run locally, and reports kernel and benchmark outcomes rather than provider economics.

entries.name: MISA routed indexer heads

public_claims.statement: The authors report query-dependent routing across DSA indexer heads, LongBench parity on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 with fewer active heads, and about 3.82x indexer-kernel speedup on one H200.

entries.competitive_implication: Reducing indexer-head work through learned or training-free routing is an occupied GLM-adjacent model-and-kernel lever.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The result is author-reported on GLM-5 rather than GLM-5.2 and does not measure the target agent workload, full serving stack, or cost.

entries.name: UNIQUE page-granular sparse attention

public_claims.statement: The authors report page-granular top-k selection using per-page key statistics, training-free and sparsity-aware training paths, up to 11.4x attention-kernel speedup, and at least 5.3x end-to-end decode speedup on their evaluated models.

entries.competitive_implication: Page-aware token selection already exists as a research direction, so a co-trained page-clustered GLM indexer must beat this class rather than claim page locality as new.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The reviewed result is not on GLM-5.2 or DSA, was not reproduced locally, and does not establish equivalent agent quality or cost.

entries.name: SPIN sparse-attention hierarchical KV serving

public_claims.statement: The authors report a vLLM-based page abstraction, sparse-attention-aware hierarchical KV placement, locality-aware HBM budgeting and metadata, with 1.66x to 5.66x throughput and up to 58% lower TPOT over evaluated sparse baselines.

entries.competitive_implication: Sparse attention plus tiered memory and page-aware serving is an active systems category, not an empty GLM-specific opportunity.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The study is not a local GLM-5.2 reproduction and its author-reported relative results do not yield target-provider dollars per token.

entries.name: INTRA non-contiguous token sparse-attention kernel

public_claims.statement: The authors report a token-granular sparse-attention data-movement design that loads non-contiguous global-memory tokens into contiguous shared memory and accelerates evaluated attention workloads by more than 3.3x.

entries.competitive_implication: Irregular sparse gather and coalesced staging are already explicit kernel research, so a GLM gather engine needs measured residual advantage over optimized token-granular kernels.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The result is not a GLM DSA study, was not reproduced locally, and does not validate a custom DRAM or accelerator design.

entries.name: Salca sparse-attention accelerator co-design

public_claims.statement: The authors report a dual-compression sparse-attention method, approximate top-k, analytical hardware search and a pipelined accelerator with 3.82x speedup and 74.19x energy efficiency over A100 in their study.

entries.competitive_implication: Sparse-attention ASIC co-design is already a published accelerator category, so custom DSA hardware must be compared against specialized prior art as well as GPUs.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The paper result is author-reported, not a fabricated-and-measured GLM-5.2 system, and does not establish manufacturing feasibility or delivered cost.

entries.name: NOSA locality-trained sparse KV offload

public_claims.statement: The authors report a trainable locality constraint for sparse token selection, a paired CPU-GPU offload system, near-lossless quality in their study, and up to 2.3x decode-throughput improvement over the InfLLM-V2 sparse baseline.

OpenBMB publishes an Apache-2.0 NOSA-1B checkpoint with a 28-layer, hidden-size-2048, two-KV-head architecture and custom CUDA sparse-attention code, providing a closer small-model co-design proxy than the current dense Qwen fixture.

entries.competitive_implication: Explicitly training the model for memory locality and tiered KV movement is already a released 1B-scale research pattern. It validates the direction as worth testing but removes it as a generic novelty claim.
entries.public_evidence_limit: The checkpoint's sparse path requires CUDA, its monolithic PyTorch weights were not executed locally, and neither its quality nor performance result transfers to GLM-5.2 without a frozen cross-scale experiment.

commoditized_layers.business_implication: A fast serving twin with scheduler, KV, routing, disaggregation and traces is necessary infrastructure, not a sufficient company moat.
Sweeping topology, parallelism, hardware, serving and SLA knobs is already sold or documented by incumbents.
Rust can improve iteration speed and correctness but is an implementation choice already used by DynoSim, not market differentiation.
Tuning speculation, quantization, caching, hardware and serving to workload distributions overlaps FireOptimizer and should not be the positioning.
Dimension alignment, wider operations, low precision, LatentMoE and parallel-friendly patterns are public design ideas; value must be in validated automated discovery beyond known rules.
Per-model executable bundles, kernels and compiler presets on custom silicon already exist as a vendor pattern.
Network topology and collective simulation should be integrated or reused, not treated as proprietary novelty.
Analytical mapping, cycles, memory traffic, energy and area tables are available building blocks whose assumptions still require silicon calibration.
A unified heterogeneous-serving simulator is no longer an unoccupied research category.
Vertical hardware is difficult and potentially valuable but cannot be claimed as unique; it must outperform active custom-accelerator vendors after full economics.
Accuracy, SLO, agent concurrency, power and system disclosure have external benchmark patterns; private simulator scores are not enough.

Cross-layer, temporal, hierarchical, head-routed and page-aware DSA reduction, locality-trained KV offload, irregular-gather kernels, sparse KV tiers and sparse-attention accelerators are active research categories. A defensible GLM result must show measured residual gain beyond these baselines rather than rediscover one mechanism.

surviving_wedge.hypothesis: The remaining defensible wedge is a quality-aware, error-calibrated autoresearch loop that mutates model architecture and representation, lowers each candidate through executable kernel, compiler, network, hardware, serving and input/output-token economics models, and proves that predictions transfer across model scale before custom silicon is authorized.
surviving_wedge.why_it_survives_public_source_review: The reviewed sources separately demonstrate strong serving twins, deployment search, hardware-aware model rules, per-model compilers, vertical accelerators, tensor and network simulators, validation benchmarks, and an active set of cross-layer, temporal, hierarchical, head-routed, page-aware and accelerator-specific sparse-attention mechanisms. They do not publicly establish one independently reproduced loop that closes model-quality deltas, system behavior, calibrated prediction uncertainty and customer-visible input/output-token economics across model mutations. This is a gap in reviewed evidence, not proof that competitors lack internal systems.
required_components: frozen quality and task-success gates for every model mutation
multi-fidelity simulation with measured confidence intervals and explicit unsupported claims
commodity-silicon calibration and blinded holdout prediction
agent-trajectory input/output-token economics under SLO and utilization distributions
cross-scale transfer tests from small proxy models to a GLM-class architecture
custom-hardware authorization only after a robust residual gain remains beyond incumbent-grade software

decision_gates.decision_scope: Whether the simulator can rank and predict unseen commodity-hardware deployments rather than merely fit known measurements.
measurements: TTFT, TPOT, request throughput and output-token throughput
peak and steady-state accelerator memory
inter-device and inter-node transferred bytes
loaded accelerator power and energy per input and output token
predicted versus measured input- and output-token cost
promotion_if_all: Freeze unseen validation cells spanning at least one dense, one MoE and one hybrid or nonstandard-attention model on at least two commodity accelerator generations.
Achieve median absolute percentage error at most 10% and p90 at most 20% separately for TTFT, TPOT, throughput, peak memory and transferred bytes.
Achieve cost prediction error at most 15%, Spearman candidate-rank correlation at least 0.90 and top-three candidate recall at least 0.80.
Demonstrate at least 80% empirical coverage for every nominal 90% simulator prediction interval.
kill_if_any: After two declared calibration rounds, any key performance metric retains median error above 20% on blinded cells.
Candidate-rank correlation remains below 0.70 or the simulator repeatedly promotes configurations that violate memory or SLO constraints.
Prediction intervals remain materially miscalibrated, making search rankings unauditable.
decision_gates.kill_action: Stop predictive co-design claims and narrow the product to measurement orchestration or profiling until a new fidelity method passes a fresh blinded protocol.
decision_gates.current_evidence_gap: No blinded multi-model, multi-accelerator silicon calibration with cost, power and network observables has been completed.

decision_gates.decision_scope: Whether joint model and vertical-stack search adds material value beyond incumbent-grade independent tuning of serving, quantization, speculation and hardware mapping.
measurements: quality- and SLO-controlled dollars per million input tokens
quality- and SLO-controlled dollars per million output tokens
input/output weighted cost for a frozen agent-trajectory mix
factorial ablation of model, kernel, serving and hardware levers
promotion_if_all: Compare against separately tuned vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM-class baselines with the same model, hardware budget, quality gates and agent SLOs.
On at least two model families, reduce measured output-token cost by at least 30% and input-token cost by at least 20%, with a paired 95% interval excluding zero regression.
Show through locked factorial ablation that cross-layer interactions contribute at least half of the gain rather than a single already-standard quantization, speculation or serving knob.
Retain the result after the baseline receives the same fixed search budget and current public optimization techniques.
kill_if_any: Best joint candidates improve the frozen weighted cost by less than 15% on both model families after the declared search budget.
The advantage disappears when the baseline uses current incumbent-grade tuning or when quality and tail-latency gates are enforced.
A single commodity optimization explains at least 80% of the observed gain.
decision_gates.kill_action: Reject vertical co-design as the moat and pivot to a narrower simulator, benchmarking or optimization-integration product.
decision_gates.current_evidence_gap: Current local mechanisms are conditional bounds or proxy-quality results and have not produced measured input/output-token cost against a fully tuned provider-grade baseline.

decision_gates.decision_scope: Whether hypotheses discovered cheaply on a small model transfer predictively to larger and GLM-class architectures without post-result reselection.
measurements: predicted and realized direction of performance change
predicted and realized quality delta
realized-to-predicted cost-gain ratio
required architecture-specific retuning effort
promotion_if_all: Lock at least three model or hardware changes using only the small-model environment before evaluating a larger model.
Across at least two scale jumps and one GLM-class or structurally comparable MoE model, predict the gain direction correctly for at least 80% of locked changes.
For passing changes, keep realized gain between 0.5x and 1.5x of the predicted gain while all frozen quality gates pass.
Demonstrate that transfer does not require changing the selection criterion after larger-model results are visible.
kill_if_any: More than one third of locked hypotheses reverse direction at larger scale or fail quality gates.
Useful results require model-specific manual retuning extensive enough to eliminate the claimed autoresearch leverage.
The small-model simulator cannot represent the dominant larger-model communication, routing or memory bottleneck.
decision_gates.kill_action: Stop treating the small model as a business-valid proxy and either fund a representative calibration platform or limit claims to the tested model class.
decision_gates.current_evidence_gap: No locked small-to-large transfer experiment or GLM-class measured execution has been completed.

decision_gates.decision_scope: Whether custom hardware adds a robust residual system and economic gain after the best model and software candidate on commodity accelerators.
measurements: post-place-and-route or equivalently grounded frequency, area and power
memory capacity, bandwidth, interconnect and package feasibility
FPGA, RTL or cycle-model system performance including compiler and serving overhead
NRE, yield, package, rack, power and utilization sensitivity
amortized input/output-token cost and payback volume
promotion_if_all: After commodity software and model optimization, retain at least a 2x simulated system opportunity attributable to hardware changes.
Validate at least a 1.5x end-to-end gain in an FPGA, RTL, emulation or independently calibrated cycle model that includes compiler, network, memory and serving overhead.
Close timing, area, power, capacity, interconnect, package and rack constraints with explicit uncertainty.
Show at least 30% amortized token-cost reduction across conservative utilization, energy-price, yield, volume and NRE sensitivity cases.
kill_if_any: Grounded realization falls below 1.5x end-to-end or software improvements consume more than half of the supposed custom-hardware advantage.
The design fails timing, memory, package, power or network feasibility at the target model scale.
Token-cost advantage depends on a single optimistic utilization, yield, volume or power assumption.
decision_gates.kill_action: Keep custom silicon and tapeout out of the company plan; continue only the software and model co-design path if its independent gate passes.
decision_gates.current_evidence_gap: No physical implementation, FPGA or RTL validation, foundry quote, package design, yield model or robust NRE amortization supports a tapeout.

decision_gates.decision_scope: Whether measured gains survive standardized agentic workloads, external reruns and initial customer willingness to pay.
measurements: MLPerf-style frozen accuracy, load generation, system disclosure and loaded power
AA-AgentPerf-style concurrent agents, TTFT, output speed and output throughput
per-accelerator, per-system and per-MW results
customer-trace cost and SLO replay
paid design-partner conversion and forecast-error tolerance
promotion_if_all: Pass frozen model-quality and agent-task gates under MLPerf-style result checking and power measurement.
Pass at least two AA-AgentPerf-style SLO tiers on real multi-turn coding traces and disclose full system configuration.
Obtain one blinded third-party or customer rerun within 15% of predicted cost and performance.
Secure at least three trace-sharing design partners and two paid pilots where prediction accuracy or realized savings is the purchased outcome.
kill_if_any: Gains disappear on multi-turn agent trajectories, long context, cache reuse or tail-latency constraints.
No external rerun lands within 25% of the simulator after two calibration cycles.
Fewer than two customers will pay for the validated outcome after a declared discovery period.
decision_gates.kill_action: Do not position as a provider competitor; reconsider whether the durable product is a research tool, services engagement or no business.
decision_gates.current_evidence_gap: Neither MLPerf nor AA-AgentPerf has been run locally, no independent rerun exists, and no paid design-partner evidence is recorded.

required_measurements: frozen accuracy or task-quality validation before performance
LoadGen-equivalent server, offline or interactive request scheduling and latency
full system and software configuration disclosure
loaded power where energy or cost is claimed
validation_targets.use_in_foundry: Adopt the methodology controls for every commodity and custom-hardware comparison; do not call an internal analogous run an MLPerf result.

required_measurements: real multi-turn coding trajectories with reasoning and tool calls
sustained concurrent agents under model-specific TTFT and output-speed SLO tiers
system output tokens per second and maximum concurrent agents
normalization per accelerator, per system and per MW using measured loaded accelerator power
validation_targets.use_in_foundry: Use as the primary external shape for the assumed agent-heavy demand mix and as a kill test for uniform synthetic-trace optimizations.

conclusion.current_decision: Continue only as a falsification-led co-design evidence program; do not pitch a generic end-to-end simulator, Rust implementation, per-model compiler, workload optimizer or vertical hardware stack as the moat.
conclusion.strongest_negative_evidence: Every major layer of the original thesis is either commercially occupied, publicly documented or available as an open research building block; even GLM-adjacent DSA reduction, locality-trained sparse KV offload, sparse-memory serving, irregular-gather kernels and sparse-attention accelerator co-design are active research categories with released small-model artifacts.
conclusion.strongest_remaining_opportunity: An independently validated closed loop that discovers non-obvious model-plus-hardware changes beyond published sparse-attention baselines, predicts quality and economics with calibrated error, transfers across scale, and proves residual gain beyond incumbent-grade software.
